reading.body:
Luis Correa's AI record is mostly money and cosponsorships, not floor leadership: 17 dated events, of which 10 are campaign contributions and 4 are recorded votes.

The contributions come from the political committees of Meta, Google, Microsoft, and Amazon, in amounts between $1,000 and $2,500, spread from March 2025 through June 2026. Google's committee appears five times, more than any other donor. The legislative side is thinner and later: two cosponsorships on the same day in July 2026, one on adversarial threats and security risks and one on frontier model oversight, plus a biometrics privacy bill in January 2026. The four recorded votes are all yea votes on suspension motions, a procedure used for bills with broad support, so they say little about where he stands on contested AI questions.

For AI specifically, the pattern matters because the bills he attached his name to are the ones that would shape how frontier models are evaluated and reported on. The donor list is the same set of companies whose data centers, power contracts, and model deployments the oversight bills would touch. Money from those committees and cosponsorship of those bills appear in the same record, but the dates do not establish that either caused the other, and the page states no conclusion about motive.

What this does not cover: there is no data here on committee assignments, floor speeches, amendments, or votes on contested AI legislation. Ten contributions and four suspension votes are a narrow slice of a member's record, and the absence of an event is not evidence of anything.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Luis Correa: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 17 events.
